1) The present revision petition has been filed by the petitioners assailing the order dated 29.01.2020 passed by the Ld. ACMM (East) in CC No. 4277/2018 titled as Kaman Kumar Vaid Vs Umashankar Sharma & Anr., whereby the Ld. ACMM issued summons to the petitioners for the offence punishable u/s 452/380/34 & 120B IPC.
2) Facts in brief are that the complainant claimed himself to be the owner of house no. B17,
Acharya Niketan, Delhi110091.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is alleged that the alleged persons as mentioned in the complaint committed offence punishable under section 452/354/380/120B/506/34 IPC in respect of the said house and members of the family of the complainant on 15.05.2002.
It was also stated in the complaint that an FIR bearing no. 135/2002 had been lodged by the said alleged persons at PS Trilok Puri for offences u/s 447/448/506/34 IPC.
A report was called from the police by the Ld.M.M. and during presummoning inquiry, the complainant examined six witnesses.
CR No. 77/2020 Page 2 of 10 ASJ04/KKD/Delhi 3) It is urged by ld.

Counsel for the petitioners that even though the complainant has claimed himself to be the owner of the property bearing no. B17, Acharya Niketan, Delhi, however, despite 18 years of the alleged incident, no civil suit has been filed by respondent no. 2 or any of his family members for possession of the property in question, which shows that the respondent does not have any right, title or interest or possession of the property in question.

It is stated that FIR No. 135/02,
PS Pandav Nagar, is concerning the property in issue regarding which FIR has been registered against respondent no. 2, his father Shahdev Raj Vaid, and brother Ramankant Vaid.

It is also urged that Smt. Sushma Sharma had admittedly been the owner and in exclusive possession of the property in issue bearing no. B17, Acharya Niketan, Mayur Vihar, PhaseI, Delhi, as also admitted by the parents of respondent no. 2 namely Sahdev Raj Vaid and Smt. Raj Rani @ Rajni in civil proceedings initiated by third persons against them and petitioners namely Umashankar and Smt.
Sushma Sharma.

It is stated that Smt. Sushma Sharma had been paying House Tax and electricity bills for the property till 11.04.2002 when respondent no. 2 and his father (now deceased) and brother tried to grab the property from Umashankar and Smt. Sushma Sharma and they also committed forgery and cheating by fabrication of false rent agreements in respect of the property in issue.

On that account on 11.04.2002 FIR No. 135/02 PS Trilok Puri was registered and charges were framed against respondent no. 2 and his brother u/s CR No. 77/2020 Page 3 of 10 ASJ 04/KKD/Delhi 451/323/356/34 & 420/468/471 r/w Section 120B IPC.
The said matter is at the stage of prosecution evidence, hence, there was no possibility of commission of the offence as alleged by the respondents in respect of the said property.
The present complaint has been filed as a counter blast to FIR No. 135/2002, PS Trilokpuri.
It is argued that none of the abovesaid facts have been considered by the Ld. A.C.M.M. while passing the impugned order dated 29.01.2020.

It is urged that the impugned order dated 29.01.2020 is in teeth of the order dated 20.08.2018 passed by the Hon'ble Delhi High Court wherein the Hon'ble High Court had directed the concerned M.M. to take into account to pass the order of summoning only after hearing the complainant and perusal of the material available on record.

It is urged that the ld. M.M. has passed the impugned order without taking into consideration the other material available on record and has also relied upon the statements of the witnesses examined by the complainant before passing the summoning order.
It is accordingly prayed that the impugned order dated 29.01.2020 may be set aside.

2 4)

On the other hand, it is contended by ld. Counsel for the respondent no. 2 that para 17 of the order of the Hon'ble High Court implies that the observations made therein by the Hon'ble High Court were suggestive in nature and not in the nature of directions to the Trial Court.

It is stated that directions cannot be given to the Trial Court to decide the issue of passing a CR No. 77/2020 Page 4 of 10 ASJ04/KKD/Delhi summoning order u/s 204 Cr.P.C., which power solely vests with the Trial Court.

It is stated that from the facts and circumstances of the present case, prima facie a case is made out against the petitioners and hence, taking of cognizance by the Ld. M.M. cannot be interfered with.
It is stated that it is not the condition precedent to issue process that the court necessarily must hold an enquiry as envisaged u/s 202 Cr.P.C. or direct investigation.
It is accordingly prayed that there is no infirmity in the order passed by the Ld. M.M. and the revision petition is liable to be dismissed.
5) The present complaint case was filed on 17.05.2002 u/s 200 Cr.P.C.
Vide the order dated 05.06.2002, the application of the complainant u/s 156(3) Cr.P.C. was dismissed and an enquiry was conducted u/s 200 Cr.
P.C. Thereafter, vide order dated 08.05.2006 the complaint was dismissed.

Revision petition was filed before the court of Ld. ASJ and on 17.07.2006, the Ld. ASJ set aside the dismissal order and the matter was remanded back with the following observations:
"Hence, the order dated 8.5.2006 is hereby set aside whereby the complaint has been dismissed and ld. Magistrate is directed to proceed to take the prima facie view of the matter and filing of the status report or the finding of the witnesses being interested or the finding that the complainant was not having any prima facie proof of ownership should not be given any consideration at this stage."
6) The matter was accordingly remanded back to Ld. MM and thereafter the complaint was again dismissed by the Ld. CR No. 77/2020 Page 5 of 10 ASJ04/KKD/Delhi MM vide order dated 07.05.2008.

A revision petition was filed assailing the said order dated 07.05.2008 and the same was disposed off by the order dated 25.03.2009 passed by Ld. ASJ and it was observed as follows:
"So long as the principle of correctness is concerned, the impugned order dated 07.05.08, the directions of ld. ASJ has been fully complied with by ld.
MM therefore, it also meet out the standard of correctness and legality as well.
I have also perused the statement of CW 2 Kanchan Lata who happens the sister of revisionist and in her statement some elements of criminality has come on record.

Statement of this witness appears to have been overlooked by the court of original jurisdiction which goes to the root of the case for the just decision of dismissal or issuing of process qua accused persons.

However, in the pursuit of objective of justice, to ensure the legal certainty and legitimate expectations the impugned order 7.5.08 is set aside and the case is remanded back to the court of ld. ACMM/MM concerned with the direction to pass a fresh order on the issue of process after considering the statement of CW2 Kanchan Lata along with other collateral facts on record and complying the directions passed by the then ld. ASJ order dated 17.7.06."

7) Pursuant thereto, vide order dated 04.06.2010, the complaint was again dismissed by the Ld.
MM.

The said order was assailed before the Ld. ASJ and vide order dated 21.03.2015, the revision petition was allowed and the order dated 04.06.2010 of the Ld. MM was set aside and the Ld. ASJ directed the parties to appear before Ld. Trial Court and thereby summoning the petitioners as accused.

The said order dated 21.03.2015 was challenged before the Hon'ble Delhi High Court vide Crl. M.C. no. 1452 of 2015 and Crl. M.A. 5348 of 2015 vide which the CR No. 77/2020 Page 6 of 10 ) Umashankar vs ) State (Nct Of Delhi)

3 ASJ04/

Hon'ble Delhi High Court set aside the impugned order dated 21.03.2015 and made the following observations in para 10, 11 and 12 of the order dated 20.08.2018: "10. ....... The criminal complaint as indeed the status reports submitted by the police at the time of initial inquiry and inquiry directed by order dated 27.10.2007 have brought to the fore certain additional facts including what is referred to by the petitioners as 'admissions' in the pleadings and proceedings of the civil suit.
11.

It may be added here that there is material presented to show investigation into FIR No.
135/2002 registered at the instance of the petitioners was completed in due course and charge-sheet was laid in the court of Metropolitan Magistrate on which the complainant of the case at hand along with one another (Raman) have been summoned.

It further appears on 21.12.2009 the Metropolitan Magistrate took the said case, inter alia, against the complainant to trial by directing charge to be framed for offences punishable under sections 420/468/471 read with Section 120-B IPC and under Sections 451, 323, 356 read with Sections 34 IPC.
12.
If the summoning order were to be passed only on the basis of scrutiny of the testimony of six witnesses presented by the complainant it would lead to a one-sided view to be taken.
That is not the object of preliminary inquiry.

This is why the law confers on the court of Magistrate, the jurisdiction to "postpone" the question of issuance of process and undertake further probe in terms of Section 202 Cr.P.C."
8) The Hon'ble Delhi High Court made further observations in para 16 and 17 which are as follows:
"16.
The proceedings, in the considered view of this Court, stood vitiated by order dated 27.10.2007 of the court of magistrate.
Opting to call upon the police "to make an enquiry" was not permissible in law.
In terms of Section 202 Cr.P.C. a direction to the police could be given to not to "enquire" but "to investigate".
The investigation by the police would entail the procedure governed by Chapter XII of Cr.P.C.
No investigation in CR No. 77/2020 Page 7 of 10 ASJ04/KKD/Delhi that sense of the matter has either been ordered or secured by the Metropolitan Magistrate till date.

The order dated 27.10.2007 directing an "enquiry" being impermissible in law, the report received in its wake could also not have been acted upon.
17.
The needful correction in the course must be done now.
The impugned orders are set aside.

The question as to whether there is need for further "inquiry" by court or "investigation by police" under Section 202 Cr.P.C. is kept open for a call thereupon to be taken by the concerned Metropolitan Magistrate, after hearing the complainant and perusal of available material."
9) The petition filed before the Hon'ble Delhi High Court was disposed off with the above directions.
Accordingly, the concerned Metropolitan Magistrate was to take a call on the issue as to whether there was a need for further "Inquiry" by court or "Investigation by Police" u/s 202 Cr.P.C. after hearing the complainant and perusal of available material.

The abovesaid said observations of the Hon'ble Delhi High Court made in para 17 have to be read in context of the observations made in para 10, 11 and 12 of its order dated 20.08.2018, as reproduced hereinabove.

4 10) Perusal of the impugned order dated 29.01.2020 reveals that the Ld. MM has issued summons to accused Umashankar, Sushma Sharma, Shiv Charan @ Billu, Ishwar and Kiran Pal for offences punishable u/s 452/380/34 and section 120B IPC.

While issuing the summons, the Ld. MM referred to and discussed the presummoning evidence of CW1, CW2, CW3, CW4, CW5,
CW6 and observed that since all the alleged persons were residents of Delhi, no further inquiry was CR No. 77/2020 Page 8 of 10 ASJ04/KKD/Delhi required to be conducted by the court to decide the issue of process.

The Ld. MM further discussed the presummoning evidence of the witnesses and held that the material on record was sufficient to prima facie show that the offences punishable u/s 452/380/34 and section 120B IPC were committed by the alleged persons.

It may however, be noted that the Ld. MM in the impugned order dated 29.01.2020, has relied upon the pre summoning evidence of the six witnesses and did not take into consideration other available material on record as observed by the Hon'ble Delhi High Court in its order dated 20.08.2018.

Though, the Ld. MM has mentioned in the impugned order that he had heard the complainant and also considered the material available on record, however, there is no mention whatsoever at all as to what material was considered and the impugned order is entirely based upon the pre summoning evidence of the witnesses and hence, not in consonance with the intent and purport of the order dated 20.08.2018 passed by the Hon'ble Delhi High Court.
11) In view of the aforesaid discussions, the impugned order dated 29.01.2020 passed by the Ld.
MM is set aside.
The revision petition is accordingly allowed.

12) Parties are directed to appear before the Ld. M.M., who shall proceed with the matter as per law and complying with the order dated 20.08.2018 passed by the Hon'ble Delhi High CR No. 77/2020 Page 9 of 10 ASJ04/KKD/Delhi Court.
